correctness.rationale: The Frobenius orbit of a root of \(U^q-U-a\) has exact length \(p\), giving \(q/p\) separable degree-\(p\) factors. For \(m<p\), the finite-field reciprocal identity and the bijection \(h\mapsto\Delta_a(Yh)/(ma)\) prove \(T_m(b+a)=T_m(b)-T_{m-1}(b)\). The zero initial values then give \(T_m(na)=(-1)^m\binom{n}{m}\), while \(q^n\)-Frobenius converts the power sum at \(i=q^n-1\) into \(T_m(na)\). Thus \(D=(1-X)^n\). The standard even-character reduction contributes one explicit factor \(1-X\), so \(\operatorname{ord}_{X=1}D=1+\deg g\) and \(\deg g=n-1\). An exact \(q=25\) verifier checks the Frobenius orbit and reciprocal-sum identity, exhaustively verifies the finite-difference bijections in all four relevant degrees, and reconstructs the \(n=3\) coefficient vector, corroborating the non-prime-base case.

value.rationale: The source establishes that Goss’s magic-index degree bound fails over prime fields. Extending the mechanism to every finite field of the same characteristic materially enlarges the phenomenon and identifies the exact replacement for the source’s irreducibility input: \(q/p\) degree-\(p\) factors of \(U^q-U-a\). The theorem also gives an exact natural count \(q(q-1)/p\) of counterexample primes from the construction for each \(n\ge3\), making the extension structurally informative rather than a routine parameter change.
